title: Logarithmic Depletion of Vortex Stretching and Singularity Evasion in the 3D Navier-Stokes Equations
summary: We present a geometric-analytic mechanism for the suppression of finite-time singularities in the 3D incompressible (unforced) Navier-Stokes equations for critical point singularities exhibiting $L^{3/2, \infty}$ spatial concentration of vorticity. We demonstrate that if the vorticity direction resides locally in a logarithmically weighted space of bounded mean oscillations, $\mathrm{bmo}_{1/|\log r|}$ -- a space failing the Dini condition and thus permitting wild oscillatory defects -- the nonlinear vortex stretching is fundamentally depleted.
